definition: Helpful and Harmless Assistant with Reinforcement Learning from Human Feedback
details: Helpful and Harmless Assistant with Reinforcement Learning from Human Feedback

explainer.lead: HH-RLHF stands for Helpful and Harmless Assistant with Reinforcement Learning from Human Feedback. It matters as a named framing for training assistants to be both useful and safe.

tiers.eli5: It's a way of teaching an AI assistant two things at once: to actually help you, and to avoid saying or doing harmful things.
tiers.practitioner: Engineers apply RLHF with two objectives, helpfulness and harmlessness, which often pull against each other. A pitfall is that over-optimizing for harmlessness can make the model refuse or hedge on legitimate requests.
tiers.paperLevel: The term names a reinforcement-learning-from-human-feedback setup for training an assistant against helpful and harmless objectives; the given definition provides no further formula or bounds.

explainer.example: An assistant is trained with human preference feedback scored on both helpfulness and harmlessness, and reviewers notice it becomes safer but more evasive on borderline questions.
